Motors are off on boot, off after a crash, and off
whenever GPIO20 floats. Fit the pull-down at the
TB6612 end, not at the Pi. Confirm with a meter
that STBY reads low with Pi-M unpowered, before
the VM lead is ever fitted.
At the fuse: 6.65 A of 7.5 A
5 V rail — 2.60 A peak of a 5 A buck
3.3 V pins 1, 17 → sensors, encoders, TB6612 VCC
mic and amp share one I²S bus: custom
Shifters run on 5 V so DIN sees a true 5 V logic
high. OE1 to GND; unused inputs to GND and
unused OE pins to VCC. 0.1 µF at each VCC.
Data is SPI0 MOSI, not PWM: PWM0/1 are the motors.
3-pin JST-XH 2.54 per string: 5 V, DIN, GND.
ground. Do not tie to star.
GND → star on its own 18 AWG conductor
1 L shoulder, 2 R shoulder, 3 head yaw,
4 head nod, 5 box tilt, 6 brow roll
GND — drawn as a bus, wired as a single star point on the distribution board. Every return above lands here and nowhere else.

svg.text: Servos are regulated, never battery-direct. A full 2S pack sits at 8.4 V and the SCS0009 maximum is 7.4 V. The 6 V buck is set off-load and marked before a servo is ever connected.
One star ground. Motor return, servo return and each converter return get their own 18 AWG conductor to the distribution board. Signal returns reach it through their Pi. Nothing daisy-chains.
STBY holds motors off on boot, after a crash and whenever GPIO20 floats. The 100 kΩ pull-down is fitted at the TB6612 end and is not optional on the robot, whatever the bench drawing says.
Logic is 3.3 V. TB6612 VCC and both encoder supplies come off the Pi-M header, so every logic and encoder output is GPIO-safe. The TB6612 reverse protection covers VM only, not VCC.
Fuse before switch, 7.5 A blade and not fast-blow. Worst-case simultaneous draw at the fuse is 6.65 A, an 11 % margin; three bulk capacitors charging at switch-on is why the blade type matters.
Build order and the full net notes are in docs/HARDWARE_power_harness.md. Do not wire from this drawing alone; the build order exists so nothing is live before it should be.
